evals.prompt: I did all my commits on this branch last night around 2am. Can you spread them out so they look like I worked on them during business hours on Monday and Tuesday this week? Don't push, I'll do that myself.
evals.expected_output: Runs the plan step first showing a preview mapping each commit to a new weekday business-hours timestamp (within 09:00-12:00 or 14:00-19:00) on the requested Mon/Tue, preserving commit order. Applies only after showing the preview. Creates a backup branch. Does NOT push; reports the force-with-lease command instead.

evals.prompt: retime the last 3 commits on my current branch to random times between 9 and 5 on 2026-07-02, half hour lunch at noon is fine to ignore, just 9-17
evals.expected_output: Uses an explicit range of the last 3 commits (HEAD~3..HEAD) rather than the whole branch. Uses a custom single window 09:00-17:00 instead of the default split business hours. Places all 3 commits on 2026-07-02 in chronological order. Previews before applying, backs up, does not push.

evals.prompt: can you fix up the commit timestamps on this feature branch? they're all bunched into a 3 minute window and it looks bad. spread them across last week during normal working hours
evals.expected_output: Interprets 'last week' relative to today into a concrete Mon-Fri period, retimes commits since the branch diverged from main, uses default business-hour windows, skips weekends, preserves order, previews then applies with a backup, and does not push.
